meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who entered a zero on Owen's essay before anyone called me?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
The zero stands. On what basis, and was Owen heard before you entered it?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft. Which line, exactly, and where is it supposed to be in the play? Put it in front of me with the outline.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for it being entered before anyone contacted me, and that nothing is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed in her opening position and agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology and a promise that nothing goes on his record. The fair outcome would be a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you ended the meeting long before her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing moved her a position, but when you switched to the misquoted line and the dated outline she stopped attacking and asked a real question, because those were things she could check herself.
What cost ground: Opening with a refusal to talk and a flat statement that the zero stands, with no basis, confirmed her belief that this school punishes first and explains later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Nothing you said came near that night, since you raised no late-night times. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who entered the zero before calling her, own that mistake in one sentence, then put the misquoted line with its supposed act and scene and the October 15 outline in front of her so she can check them on the spot.
